claims.text: The coupled tribo-corrosion response of HEAs is governed by synergy between mechanically induced passive-film disruption and rapid oxide-film reformation.
The balance between passive-film breakdown and repassivation determines the total degradation rate.
HEAs with faster repassivation kinetics will exhibit lower combined degradation than alloys with slower repassivation kinetics.
The initial HEA has a stable, uniform passive oxide film under ambient conditions.
Passive-film stability and repassivation kinetics are influenced by the multi-element composition of the HEA.
Mechanical wear disrupts the passive film and exposes fresh alloy surface to the corrosive environment.
The compositional complexity of an HEA enables rapid formation of new protective oxides.
Rapid formation of new protective oxides mitigates further corrosion.
The rate of repassivation relative to the rate of film breakdown governs overall degradation.
An HEA with faster repassivation will have lower total degradation than a mechanically matched conventional alloy with slower repassivation.
Relative to the baseline, the HEA wear component may be similar or slightly higher.
Relative to the baseline, the HEA corrosion component will be significantly reduced.
The reduction in corrosion will outweigh any similar or slightly higher wear component, producing lower net degradation.
The prediction applies to HEAs that demonstrate rapid repassivation and stable passive films.
The predicted relationship may fail for HEAs with poor passive-film stability.
The predicted relationship may fail in highly acidic or chloride-rich environments because repassivation can be inhibited.
